newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks seen steady at open.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks seen steady at open.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to open generally steady, pausing for a brief respite ahead of Friday's critical payrolls and unemployment figures.
Analysts said the market could face profit-taking ahead of the Friday report but doubted any serious selling pressure was ahead for stocks.
"Valuations are high and I'm looking for a cautious session, a day of reflection," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments. "I do expect some profit-taking."

Weekly jobless claims figures are due at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT. Economists expect 341,000 new claims, roughly flat versus 340,000 last week. August factory orders, expected to decline by 1.2 percent, will be released at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT.
Absent a major surprise in the reports, analysts said the market would likely bide time until reviewing tomorrow's figues.
"I think you'll see some tired blood out there but people will want to get in on any kind of dip," said Larry Wachtel, market analyst at Prudential Securities.
In Tokyo, stocks settled lower in a quiet session. The Nikkei-225 index fell 167 points to 21,332.
U.S. stocks were steady to slightly higher in London, but caution ahead of Friday's economic data held stocks in check. The FTSE-100 fell 17 points to 3998, dipping back below the 4000 mark.
The dollar retreated in Tokyo after an early run at the 112 yen level and eased to just above the 1.53 mark level in Europe.
The 30-year U.S. Treasury rose 8/32 to yield 6.82 percent.
The December S&P 500 index future fell 0.3 to 699.2.
The New York Times Marketplace column focuses on the Federal Reserve's apparent ability to take small risks on the inflation front due to its heightened credibitilty in the capital markets.
A decline in gold prices may have created some bargains among shares in gold mining companies, the Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column reports.
